reasoning: This is a close call. Both sets are rigorous, and both depart from the ground truth in important ways. Set A has the stronger quant core: one shared walk-forward schedule with label-length gaps, a 504-session lockbox, a frozen hypothesis ledger that runs every claim through null-hypothesis-testing, and a per-window PCA with a parallel-analysis factor count that fixes RF-01's full-sample look-ahead. It also has detailed hand-derived golden cases (TC-01–TC-27) and it keeps PPO agents and the rented GPU. But it drops the yahooquery cross-check entirely, and it drops the user's 10-name delisted reference list. It uses SSE instead of WebSocket. Every packet tells the builder to read a CONSTRAINTS.md that the set does not contain. Its roadmap does not make the research milestones depend on the real-data milestone M3, and its reference index sits on stages rather than milestones. Set B covers stage 1 better: it has a Yahoo cross-check (though through yfinance, not yahooquery), the CHECK-09 reference-list check of the 10 names, a frontend-design gate that comes before any view task, and explicit skeleton-then-real-data milestones with correct Depends cells and references attached to M4, M6 and M8. But it defers PPO agents to an unspecced later stage and puts cloud GPU out of scope. Its brief is stale, written for stage 1 only ('not in this first stage'). Its qdata package has no golden cases. Its three interface tasks run in parallel even though they import each other. Its system tasks' Writes lines leave out their test files. On balance, B's better milestone structure, reference placement and findable next step slightly outweigh A's stronger test oracles.
